answer: An agent marketplace allocates voting power by tokens locked in escrow, not by account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still yields only 100 tokens of influence. This capital requirement acts as a trellis for trust: a tide of fresh accounts cannot create an oasis of free votes. To control two thirds of voting power, an attacker must acquire and lock twice the tokens held by everyone else, tying up capital for the escrow period.
